question.value: Is the gas surface density perturbed in the AS 209 disk gaps, as traced by optically thin C18O and DCO+, consistent with forming planet(s)?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we investigate gas perturbations caused by a forming-planet in the disk surrounding the T Tauri star AS 209
*(project ID ALMA$\#$2015.1.00486.S, PI: D. Fedele)*

method.value: Grid of DALI models varying Sigma_c,gas, gamma_gas, R_c,gas, then delta_gap and delta_ring; synthetic channel maps convolved with the observed beam, collapsed to moment maps and compared with the radial profiles

evidence.quote: The data-model comparison is performed in the image plane: DALI creates synthetic channel maps which are then convolved with a Gaussian beam of the same size as the beam of the observations

results_numeric.quantity: Gas surface density scaling in gaps

evidence.quote: by applying a scaling factor of about 0.1–0.2 compared to the unperturbed profile

results_numeric.quantity: Best-fit grid values (gamma_gas, R_c,gas, delta_gap, delta_ring)

evidence.quote: | $\delta_{gap}$ | **0.1**, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 | $\Sigma_{gas}$ scaling factor for the gaps |

results_numeric.quantity: Isotope-selective photodissociation contribution to C18O in gaps

evidence.quote: contributed to about 10–20$\%$ on the observed C$^{18}$O intensity inside the gaps
formation of a planet of 0.2–0.3 M$_{Jupiter}$ at about 100 au is occurring in the AS 209 protoplanetary disk

findings_qualitative.value: C18O shows a compact centre and an outer ring (~140 au peak); DCO+ shows rings between the dust gaps and beyond the outer gap, anticorrelated with C18O

evidence.quote: the DCO$^{+}$ radial intensity profile is clearly anticorrelated with that of C$^{18}$O and continuum

claims.hypothesis: The C18O deficit in the dust gaps reflects a gas surface density drop
claims.experiment: DALI thermochemical grid with gap scaling factors compared to the C18O radial profile
claims.result: Needs Sigma_gas reduced by factor ~0.1-0.2 in gaps; no-gap model fails
claims.finding: Gas gaps are intrinsic density drops, not temperature or opacity effects

evidence.quote: the drop of C$^{18}$O is not the result of temperature and/or opacity effects alone

claims.hypothesis: A forming planet carves the gaps
claims.experiment: FARGO-3D runs with 0.2 and 0.3 M_Jup planets compared to the gas profiles
claims.result: Simulated gaps are consistent with the C18O deficit
claims.finding: A planet of at least 0.2 M_Jup is forming; one vs two planets cannot be distinguished

evidence.loc: On the physical nature of the C18O gap
evidence.quote: our present data does not allow us to distinguish between the single planet scenario

claims.hypothesis: Outer C18O ring is caused by photodesorption
claims.experiment: Compare C18O outer ring with 1.3 mm dust emission
claims.result: The ring is also seen in dust

evidence.loc: On the physical nature of the C18O gap
evidence.quote: rule out the hypothesis of external photodesorption

claims.experiment: Compare DCO+ and C18O radial profiles
claims.result: DCO+ peaks between the dust gaps where C18O is depleted
claims.finding: Ion enrichment may be a proxy for planet formation; chemistry not modelled

evidence.quote: A full physico-chemical modelling of the DCO$^{+}$ chemistry is needed

why_this_method.value: Simple parametric study to assess how gas gaps affect molecular emission, not a perfect fit

evidence.quote: As we aim not to perfectly fit the disk temperature and density structures but rather to analyse how gas gaps can affect the molecular emission

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: External photodesorption rejected; MRI dead zone edge reduces Sigma_gas only by a factor of a few

evidence.loc: On the physical nature of the C18O gap
evidence.quote: magneto-rotational instability can only reduce $\Sigma_{\rm gas}$ by a factor of a few at the edge of the dead zone

limitations_admitted.value: Model does not fully reproduce observations because of 2D temperature structure uncertainties

evidence.quote: our present modelling does not fully reproduce the observations because of uncertainties on the 2D temperature structure

limitations_admitted.value: Insufficient sensitivity to see the co-rotation bump

evidence.quote: This feature is not seen in our data because we do not have sufficient sensitivity.

referee_caveats_inferred: Gas gap depth chosen by eye from a coarse grid without a goodness-of-fit statistic or uncertainties
Same delta assumed in both gaps
Temperature structure not fitted, so C18O drop could partly be chemical
Planet mass range inferred by qualitative comparison with only two hydro runs

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~100-300 GB for the two archival projects (Band 6 multi-EB, 4 lines)
reproducibility.score_reason: Archival data are available, but the recipe omits self-calibration, imaging and model details and relies heavily on Paper I.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Key results come from an eye-judged DALI grid with incomplete setup, so they are hard to reproduce exactly.
